chunks: Harun ibn Hamzah al-Ghanawi narrated from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام:
Regarding a man who died and had not performed the Hajj of Islam, and he left behind nothing except the amount of the expenses of Hajj, and he had heirs.
He عليه السلام said: "They have greater right to his inheritance. If they wish, they may consume it, and if they wish, they may perform Hajj on his behalf."

key_terms.حَجَّةَ الْإِسْلَامِ: the obligatory Hajj incumbent in Islam
key_terms.حَجُّوا عَنْهُ: perform Hajj on his behalf after his death
key_terms.مِيرَاثِهِ: his estate or inheritance left behind
key_terms.نَفَقَةِ الْحَجِّ: the financial cost and expenses of performing Hajj
key_terms.وَرَثَةٌ: legal heirs entitled to inherit from the deceased

ai.seo_question: If someone dies without performing Hajj and leaves only enough money for Hajj, do the heirs inherit it or must it be spent on Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about a deceased person who did not perform the obligatory Hajj and left only enough wealth to cover its expenses. It states that when heirs remain and there was no more than that amount, the heirs have the stronger claim to the inheritance and may choose either to keep it or to perform Hajj on his behalf.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2917 - Harun ibn Hamzah al-Ghanawi narrated from Abu Abdullah (as)
regarding a man who died without performing the Hajj of Islam and left behind only enough wealth for the expenses of Hajj, and he had heirs.
Imam (as) said: "They have the greater right to his inheritance. If they wish, they may use it for themselves, and if they wish, they may perform Hajj on his behalf."
